summary.title: High Scalability
summary.one_liner: A blog index of system architecture and scalability articles, including guest posts and reposts on Kafka, AWS S3, Uber, Presto, gossip protocol, and consistent hashing.
takeaways: Kafka was developed at LinkedIn in 2011 and is an open-source Apache project (intro article 'Kafka 101').
Gossip protocols address liveness and state maintenance in distributed systems; consistent hashing distributes data across nodes.
Meta ran Presto, a free open-source SQL query engine, at scale for about ten years and shared four lessons learned.
Outages can be caused by unapproved changes, as the Swedbank April 2022 outage showed.
summary.summary: This is the front page of High Scalability, a blog that collects articles on building large, fast, reliable websites and systems. The listing shows a mix of guest posts and reposts (for example from ByteByteGo and Uber engineering leaders) plus the blog's own weekly scalability roundup and sponsored posts. Topics include Kafka basics, how AWS S3 handles scale, the history of scaling Uber, Presto at Meta, gossip protocol, consistent hashing, and a case study on the Swedbank outage. The page is an index, so each entry is only a short excerpt and the full detail lives in the linked articles.
